headline: Not verified: Gateway runs in a genuine Intel TDX enclave; Your report was encrypted to the attested gateway; Model runs in a genuine Intel TDX enclave; Model GPUs are in confidential-computing mode; Analysis was signed inside the model enclave.

properties.title: Gateway runs in a genuine Intel TDX enclave
properties.statement: The NEAR AI Cloud gateway that received the request runs measured software inside an Intel TDX confidential VM, and produced this evidence after our challenge.

checks.detail: Attestation report unavailable (HTTP 503): “Provider error: No provider found that supports attestation reports for model: openai/gpt-5.4”.

properties.title: Your report was encrypted to the attested gateway
properties.statement: The TLS session carrying the report terminated inside the attested gateway enclave, not at an intermediary. The peer certificate and socket identity are observed live by the backend that captured this evidence; offline re-verification checks them against the quote but cannot re-observe the connection.

checks.label: TLS key is inside the attested TEE
Report sent over the attested connection

properties.title: Model runs in a genuine Intel TDX enclave
properties.statement: The model-serving environment runs measured software in an Intel TDX confidential VM, bound to the signing key, and answered our fresh challenge.

checks.label: Model attestation present
checks.detail: No model-TEE attestation candidates were returned.

properties.title: Model GPUs are in confidential-computing mode
properties.statement: NVIDIA attested — and signed a verdict bound to our nonce — that the GPUs serving the model are genuine and running in confidential-computing mode with expected firmware.

checks.label: GPU evidence present
checks.detail: No model-TEE attestation candidates were returned.

properties.title: Analysis was signed inside the model enclave
properties.statement: The model TEE signed SHA-256 hashes of the exact request we sent and the exact response we received, with a key that the attested hardware vouches for; the attestation challenge was derived from that same request.

checks.label: Response signature available

not_proven: That the model’s security analysis is correct. AI triage is a recommendation; attestation proves how it ran, not what it concluded.
That NEAR AI Cloud does not retain prompts. Attestation identifies measured software; it does not audit retention behaviour of that software.
End-to-end encryption to the model. TLS terminates in the attested gateway TEE; the gateway then forwards to the model TEE over a channel this receipt does not verify.
Image provenance. Container digests are measured and displayed, but not checked against a source-build allowlist.
That the verified model report and the completion came from the same serving instance (instances of one model share a signing key).
Confidentiality between the user’s browser and the PrivateTriage backend beyond standard HTTPS/localhost.
That NEAR’s pinned software is free of vulnerabilities. Measurements identify which dstack OS image and NEAR app ran (pinned on first observation, 2026-11-13); they are not an audit of that software.
trust_assumptions: Intel TDX hardware and Intel’s attestation signing root (DCAP / PCS).
NVIDIA H100/H200 confidential-computing hardware and NVIDIA NRAS signing keys (JWKS fetched over WebPKI TLS).
The measured NEAR AI Cloud software stack (dstack, gateway, model server) behaves as its published source describes.
The PrivateTriage backend you run: it holds the API key, sees your report in plaintext, and performs these checks.
WebPKI for the TLS connections to Intel PCS, NVIDIA NRAS and NEAR AI Cloud.
